source.question: F-12's water cut fell from about 0.97 to about 0.3 at the end of 2014. What was done to the well, and why did the plug set in 2010 not do the same?

submission.summary: F-12’s water cut fell from about 97% in October 2014 to about 31% in January 2015 most likely because the well was shut in and re-completed: a plug was set higher at 3150 m to shut off the water interval around 3126 m and a new oil zone was perforated, consistent with the timing and water-cut drop. The 2010 plug set deeper at 3210 m could only block a small fraction of the water, so it did not cut the water cut.

findings.claim: F-12’s monthly water cut fell from about 97% in October 2014 to about 31% in January 2015 after a month-long shut-in.
findings.detail: production_monthly E2: 2014-10 water_cut 0.9665, oil 5386 Sm3, water 155366 Sm3; 2014-11 water_cut 0.9623; 2014-12 0 days, 0 oil; 2015-01 water_cut 0.3107, oil 25713 Sm3. detect_events E3: shut in 32 days from 2014-11-30, rate 185 -> 860 Sm3/d (+366%) after restart.

findings.claim: At the end of 2014 the well was worked over: a 7-inch plug was set at 3150 m and a new zone was perforated from 3126.2 to 3130.7 m MD.
findings.detail: well_operations E4 jobs start 2014-11-22, summary: Installed 7" EV0 plug with mid element at 3150 m. Perforated new zone from 3126,2 -3139,7 mMD. well_operations day E8 2014-11-26: Correlated BHA, Set plug with mid packer element at 3150 m, Positioned gun with top shot at 3126,2 m & bottom shot at 3130,7 mMD.

findings.claim: In September 2010 a plug had been set deeper at 3210 m.
findings.detail: well_operations E4 jobs start 2010-09-20, well_operations day E7 2010-09-23: Installed 5,72" EVO bridge plug at 3210 m mid element, top plug at 3209,3 m; operations at depth_mmd 3210.

findings.claim: The 2010 plug could only block about 33% of the water and about 1% of the oil, while the 2014 plug blocks about 97% of the water.
findings.detail: production_log E6 PLT 2010-09 low rate: below 3210 m oil_share 0.011, water_share 0.325; medium rate oil_share 0.015, water_share 0.376; below 3150 m low rate oil_share 0.808, water_share 0.971; medium rate oil_share 0.734, water_share 1.0. Water comes in 3165-3243 m, oil 3132-3165 m. So most water entered above 3210 but below 3150.

result.note: Daily reports exist for drilling and for work on the well (wireline, plugs, perforations, production logs), not for days of normal production. A job's date is the day the work was done; kind is drilling, completion, workover (work on a producing or injecting well) or abandonment. Ask for one day to see every operation line.

result.note: A production log measures the flow passing each depth while the well flows; going up, it grows past each zone that produces. A share at a depth is the part of the pass's oil or water entering below that depth (1 at the bottom of the well's inflow, 0 above the top zone). comes_in_from_m to to_m holds 90% of each phase's inflow. Only shares are given: the files' rates have no units, and the plots' are downhole volumes. A plug set at a depth shuts off what enters below it: the shares below say what it could remove. Each survey's passes were run at several surface rates. A survey read off pictures carries the checks of that reading.

result.no_trend: WOR is not rising with cumulative oil on 2013-05 to 2016-08: no limit can be projected
result.notes: WOR = water/oil by month; the trend is log10(WOR) against cumulative oil, fitted on up to 36 recent months with WOR >= 1. field_voidage: replacement_ratio is injection over voidage at reservoir conditions (Bo 1.385 m3/Sm3 from PUD p.20, low/high with Bo 1.5/1.27; Bw 1; above the bubble point, so no free gas); surface_ratio is the same in surface volumes, which overstates replacement.
